content: Furthermore, forward-looking analyses emphasize the integration of artificial intelligence and emerging digital frameworks as critical trends aimed at addressing operational and environmental challenges [14] . In the realm of managed Wi-Fi, artificial intelligence is increasingly utilized to automate network management, predict hardware failures, and optimize bandwidth allocation in real-time. The broader African context reveals a landscape where infrastructure improvements are ongoing, yet significant challenges remain. In May 2022, reports indicated that Sub-Saharan Africa faced persistent coverage gaps, with only 59% of the population utilizing mobile internet, thereby leaving substantial portions of the demographic entirely unconnected [25] . This regional challenge is reflective of wider, systemic barriers to connectivity that have historically concentrated high-speed infrastructure in affluent, urban centers while neglecting rural and marginalized communities. To fully understand the market position and expansion trends of South African ISPs like Bioniq, it is essential to contextualize these efforts within the global drive for digital inclusivity. Connectivity growth in underserved areas remains a critical focus worldwide, with varying levels of progress reported across different regions. For instance, in Chad, the government actively sought support from the World Bank in June 2023 to expand telecommunications infrastructure to approximately 500 underserved communities, highlighting a strong governmental commitment to unlocking economic and social development through improved digital access [21] . Similarly, in highly developed regions like California, the "Broadband For All" initiative exemplifies a massive undertaking to address digital inequities; by June 2026, the state had transitioned from conceptual planning to operational execution, aiming to bring robust broadband access to historically unserved and underserved communities [22] . Despite these advancements, global challenges persist, as highlighted in studies from 2023 which demonstrated that mobile internet adoption rates remained stagnant among marginalized groups, including rural populations, women, and persons with disabilities [1] .
